dispatch.headline: Lichen Stays, Wins Again
dispatch.body:
Baptiste Kasprzak, who has handled the winning entry since its first Best in Show, collected the Ladle on Saturday for a lichen that has not moved in four years. The Karrow Deep Dog Show drew sixty-one entries, nineteen of them dogs.

The lichen, a grey-green patch of about two hand-spans on a slab of vent rock, was admitted in 2771 after a judge, Noor Salave'a, searched the rulebook for a clause against it. She found none. "It has better coat condition and stays when told," she said at the time. She repeated it on Saturday, with the same expression.

Kasprzak rises at five to mist the rock. He walks the lichen the length of the show hall on a tray, at a pace set by the tray. "People say it never does anything," he said. "Sit, down, stay. Not once has it refused. I wish I could say that about my wife."

The runner-up, a hound named Pilot, broke from the line twice. His owner, Mehmet Fonoti, has entered for eleven years. He said he was not bitter, and that Pilot had eaten the ribbon.

The show committee will vote in spring on a rule requiring entrants to have a heartbeat. Three members have said they will vote against it. Their entries are mosses.
dispatch.scene: A man in a padded grey vent-suit walks slowly down a show-hall aisle carrying a tray with a small patch of lichen on a slab of rock, a judge in a sash watching him from a table behind.
dispatch.premise: An ice-moon settlement's annual Dog Show is won for the fourth year running by a lichen, whose entry was approved when a judge, unable to find a rule excluding it, admitted that the lichen 'has better coat condition and stays when told'.

drafts.headline: Opera Counts Eels As Subscribers
drafts.body:
Yusra Belinskaya, box-office manager at the Deepwarren Opera House, has entered 312 blind cave eels on the subscriber roll since the spring season. The eels live in the flooded orchestra pit and have attended every performance since the house reopened its authentic live audience programme.

Belinskaya logs each one by the notch pattern on its tail. "They arrive before the doors open and leave after the last curtain," she said. "Show me a human who does that."

Sponsors demand organic engagement figures each quarter. Human attendance is 41 a night. The eels bring the house to 353, and the ledger does not say which is which.

Tamsin Mwangi, chief of the pit crew, has drained the pit twice. Both times the eels returned through a vent nobody had mapped. Last month the string section asked to be moved up to the stalls, because the eels strike the water in time with the tempo and are always slightly ahead of it.

Gaukhar Szabo, a subscriber of eleven years, said she had not noticed any difference. "The seats are cheaper now," she said. "Someone is clearly paying for them."

The eels have asked for nothing. Management has put them down for the renewal letter.
drafts.premise: Beneath the ice of Europa in 2774, the Deepwarren Opera House's restored 'authentic live audience' programme is overtaken by a colony of blind cave eels that have colonised the flooded orchestra pit and now attend every performance, and the management, desperate for the 'organic engagement' numbers sponsors demand, has quietly begun counting them as subscribers.

drafts.headline: Cockroaches Praised For Staying In Character
drafts.body:
Kaveh Jovanovic, who has run the Level Nine viewing hall for thirty-one years, spent Friday morning sweeping the aisles before the 400th anniversary episode of 'Cave Wives of Level Nine'. He found the roaches already seated. The hall's sixty thousand cockroaches had arranged themselves, overnight, into two camps on either side of the central drain.

The camps match the Ridge Wives and the Pool Wives. Producers confirmed that the insects have followed the show since its first season, and that the split has held through every betrayal in the record.

"Tavita's side moved to the west wall the week Tavita's character left the cave," Jovanovic said. "I thought it was damp."

The broadcast office checked the roach lines against the scripts. They matched on 212 of 219 feuds. The seven misses were all episodes later cut for length.

Haruto Petrosyan, head of the show's writing floor, said the insects would be credited as "consistent character work" in the anniversary titles. Two human actors asked for the same line to be removed from their own credits. It was refused.

Residents were told not to step on the Pool side during the finale. Jovanovic has put down a strip of matting.

"They have never once missed a reunion episode," he said. "Which is more than my sister."
drafts.premise: Residents of a buried arcology celebrate the 400th anniversary of their beloved reality show 'Cave Wives of Level Nine' after learning the cockroach population has been watching it all along, and has been steadily rearranging itself into plot-accurate rivalries, which the producers now credit as 'consistent character work'.

drafts.headline: Squid Want Two Clicks To Look
drafts.body:
Orhan Lindqvist, a gallery keeper at the Grand Aquarium, has spent nine days standing at a locked door with a bag of toll-shells nobody will take back. The Aquarium closed its viewing galleries on Monday after the exhibited squid were seen charging visitors to look at them.

The fee is two clicks, delivered against the glass in a rhythm the squid have kept constant. Visitors who did not pay were followed along the gallery by a single squid until they left. The gift shop began accepting the clicks in the second week.

"A man tapped twice on the till and got a mug," Lindqvist said. "The till was happy. I checked the till."

The Aquarium had not known the clicks were a toll until Milos Nwosu, the visiting language keeper, listened to a month of recordings. Nwosu found that the squid had been charging staff since the opening. Lindqvist, who tapped the glass most mornings to say hello, has paid for eleven years.

"I thought we were friends," he said. "It turns out I was a regular."

The squid have not commented. Last Thursday they were seen arranging a small counter of pale stones on the tank floor, one stone for each visitor still owing.
drafts.premise: Enceladus's under-ice Grand Aquarium, built to show visitors rare native fauna, shuts its viewing galleries after the exhibited squid are observed charging admission to the humans through the glass, in the form of a clicking toll that the gift shop has started to accept.

quality.judge_reason: The lichen's perfect obedience and the committee's 'Their entries are mosses' kicker land real jabs at gatekeeping, though the opening sentence already states the whole joke.
quality.critique: Headline describes the premise and the last line is a decent kicker but only half-lands; the heartbeat rule vote is stated flatly. Logic check: 'Fourth year running' fits 2771 admission only if the year is 2774 or later, and the Ladle quote about Kasprzak 'since its first Best in Show' is fine.

picture.reason: The loser shows the carrier in a light field shirt and wide-brimmed hat rather than a padded grey vent-suit, and he walks toward the viewer instead of slowly down the aisle.
picture.winner_faults: The judge in a sash watching from a table behind the carrier is missing; the background shows only spectators along the aisle.
